title: Diet rapidly and reproducibly alters the human gut microbiome
claim: An animal-based diet increased bile-tolerant Alistipes, Bilophila and Bacteroides in a short-term human intervention.
context: Controlled dietary change with repeated stool sampling.
deltaMeaning: Shows that these taxa can change over short intervals in response to diet. An increase or decrease here does not establish Sid’s diet or explain his change.
limits: Genus-level context. Different assay and population; no verified pipeline match. No dietary exposure is linked to these visits in this explorer.

title: Supplementation with Akkermansia muciniphila in overweight and obese human volunteers: a proof-of-concept exploratory study
claim: Pasteurized A. muciniphila supplementation improved insulin sensitivity versus placebo in an exploratory trial; 32 participants completed it.
context: Overweight/obese, insulin-resistant volunteers receiving a defined preparation.
deltaMeaning: Supplementation is different from a spontaneous change in stool abundance. This study does not establish a benefit from the observed delta.
limits: Sid’s prominent annotation is Akkermansia sp KLE1798, not A. muciniphila. Species and strain equivalence are not established; no cancer or individual-response conclusion.

title: Bacteroides uniformis CECT 7771 ameliorates metabolic and immunological dysfunction in mice with high-fat-diet induced obesity
claim: Administration of B. uniformis CECT 7771 reduced weight gain and improved selected metabolic and immune measures in a mouse obesity model.
context: High-fat-diet mice receiving a particular cultured strain.
deltaMeaning: Provides experimental context, not evidence that a rise or fall of B. uniformis in this person improves or worsens health.
limits: Mouse findings and a specific strain cannot be transferred to an SGB abundance change; the strain and its activity are not measured here.

title: Effects of diet on resource utilization by a model human gut microbiota containing Bacteroides cellulosilyticus WH2, a symbiont with an extensive glycobiome
claim: B. cellulosilyticus WH2 adapted carbohydrate utilization to dietary substrates in an experimental gut community.
context: Defined microbial communities in germ-free mice, with complementary laboratory assays.
deltaMeaning: Suggests substrate availability as a research question. The stool trajectory does not measure carbohydrate utilization or reveal its cause.
limits: Strain WH2 and a model ecosystem; neither strain identity nor gene expression is established by Sid’s abundance annotation.

title: Predicting and manipulating cardiac drug inactivation by the human gut bacterium Eggerthella lenta
claim: Digoxin inactivation was linked to a strain-variable cardiac glycoside reductase operon in E. lenta.
context: Mechanistic work on bacterial drug metabolism.
deltaMeaning: Illustrates why abundance alone is insufficient to infer metabolic activity. A delta does not measure the relevant gene or drug conversion.
limits: No digoxin exposure is asserted for Sid. Species abundance does not establish a functional strain, drug effect or treatment implication.

title: Cross-cohort gut microbiome associations with immune checkpoint inhibitor response in advanced melanoma
claim: Microbiome associations with immunotherapy response varied substantially across melanoma cohorts.
context: Patients with advanced melanoma treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors.
deltaMeaning: Conflicting cross-cohort findings caution against assigning a universal good/bad meaning to a microbial change.
limits: Different cancer and treatment context; observational response associations are not evidence about this person’s trajectory. Pipeline compatibility is not verified.
